title: Systematic investigation of the potential multi-target pharmacological mechanisms of Astragaloside IV in polycystic ovary syndrome via network pharmacology and in vivo/in vitro experiments.
authors: Feng, Ying; Wu, Lei; Liu, Jianrong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芪甲苷治疗多囊卵巢综合征的网络药理学与实验验证，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent endocrine-metabolic disorder affecting reproductive-aged women and is characterized by hyperandrogenemia, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovaries. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), an active compound derived from Astragalus membranaceus, shows promise in the treatment of metabolic disorders. However, the precise molecular targets and mechanisms of action in PCOS remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of AS-IV in PCOS. AS-IV's therapeutic effects of AS-IV were assessed in a rat model of PCOS. Potential AS-IV targets were predicted using the PharmMapper and SwissTargetPrediction databases and expanded using STRINGdb. PCOS-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)datasets, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) revealed the disease-associated gene modules. Overlapping drug-disease targets were analyzed using protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, Gene Ontology (GO), and KEGG pathway enrichment. The core targets were validated using molecular docking. In vitro, qPCR was used to assess key gene expression in the control, DHT model, AS-IV, EP300 inhibitor (C646), and Nrf2 inhibitor (ML385) groups. A total of 371 potential AS-IV targets were identified. Analysis of GEO data yielded 2286 DEGs, with WGCNA identifying key PCOS-related modules and hub genes. The intersection revealed 31 key targets, including five core genes. In vivo, AS-IV improved ovarian pathology, increased antioxidant enzyme levels, reduced inflammatory cytokine, testosterone, and LH levels, and increased estradiol levels. In vitro, the PCOS, EP300, and Nrf2 inhibitor groups showed decreased EP300, NFE2L2, HMOX1, and AKT1 expression and increased MMP9 expression compared to the controls and AS-IV group. AS-IV ameliorated endocrine and ovarian abnormalities in PCOS by modulating the EP300/Nrf2/HMOX1/MMP9 axis, demonstrating multi-target antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hormone-regulatory effects, supporting its potential as a therapeutic agent for PCOS.
abstract_zh: 多囊卵巢综合征（PCOS）是一种影响育龄女性的常见内分泌代谢性疾病，其特征为高雄激素血症、排卵功能障碍和多囊卵巢。黄芪甲苷IV（AS-IV）是从黄芪（Astragalus membranaceus）中提取的活性化合物，在代谢性疾病治疗中显示出潜力。然而，其在PCOS中的精确分子靶点和作用机制仍不清楚。本研究旨在阐明AS-IV在PCOS中的治疗效果及其潜在机制。在大鼠PCOS模型中评估了AS-IV的治疗效果。利用PharmMapper和SwissTargetPrediction数据库预测AS-IV的潜在靶点，并通过STRINGdb进行扩展。从基因表达综合数据库（GEO）数据集中识别PCOS相关的差异表达基因（DEGs），加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）揭示了疾病相关基因模块。通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络、基因本体论（GO）和KEGG通路富集分析重叠的药物-疾病靶点。核心靶点通过分子对接进行验证。在体外实验中，使用qPCR评估对照组、DHT模型组、AS-IV组、EP300抑制剂（C646）组和Nrf2抑制剂（ML385）组中的关键基因表达。共识别出371个潜在的AS-IV靶点。GEO数据分析获得2286个DEGs，WGCNA识别出关键的PCOS相关模块和枢纽基因。交集揭示31个关键靶点，包括五个核心基因。在体内实验中，AS-IV改善了卵巢病理状态，增加了抗氧化酶水平，降低了炎症细胞因子、睾酮和LH水平，并增加了雌二醇水平。在体外实验中，与对照组和AS-IV组相比，PCOS、EP300和Nrf2抑制剂组的EP300、NFE2L2、HMOX1和AKT1表达降低，而MMP9表达升高。AS-IV通过调节EP300/Nrf2/HMOX1/MMP9轴改善了PCOS中的内分泌和卵巢异常，展现出多靶点的抗氧化、抗炎和激素调节作用，支持其作为PCOS治疗药物的潜力。
